introduction.en: Poverty estimation in India has evolved from a purely nutritional focus to a broader consumption-based framework to better reflect the changing economic landscape.
introduction.hi: Poverty estimation in India has evolved from a purely nutritional focus to a broader consumption-based framework to better reflect the changing economic landscape.

body.en: The Alagh Committee (1979) set the foundation using calorie norms. The Lakdawala Committee (1993) introduced state-specific lines. The Tendulkar Committee (2009) moved away from calorie norms to a uniform basket of goods, while the Rangarajan Committee (2014) further increased the poverty line to account for non-food expenditure. These shifts have expanded the definition of poverty but remain debated regarding their adequacy.

overview.title: Expert Groups For Estimating Poverty
overview.definition: The formal institutional mechanisms and expert committees constituted by the Government of India to define poverty lines, establish measurement methodologies, and estimate poverty incidence across rural and urban sectors.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Central to Indian Economy syllabus (Human Development, Poverty, Employment). Frequently tested in Prelims through chronological ordering of committees, methodology shifts (Calorie intake vs. Multi-dimensional), and specific data points, while Mains requires evaluating inclusive growth and policy targeting.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Expert Groups For Estimating Poverty.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) surveys
Difference between absolute and relative poverty

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Poverty Line Definition**: The threshold of income or consumption expenditure required to purchase a a basket of essential goods and services necessary for basic survival and minimum standard of living.
• **Calorie-Based Origins**: Early estimation methods (Alagh Committee, 1979) focused purely on minimum nutritional requirements: **2400 kcal/person/day** for rural areas and **2100 kcal/person/day** for urban areas.
• **Shift to Consumption Expenditure**: Poverty estimation in India primarily relies on **Monthly Per Capita Consumption Expenditure (MPCE)** data collected through NSSO Consumer Expenditure Surveys.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Transition from purely nutritional adequacy to broader baskets including health, education, and non-food expenditures.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Based on nutritional requirement (2400/2100 kcal). Used state-specific poverty lines based on CPI-AL and CPI-IW.
Assumed state-specific price differentials but kept consumption basket constant over time.
Frequently asked as the baseline pre-reform methodology.
Moved away from calorie norms. Included health and education expenditure. Used Mixed Reference Period (MRP).
Estimated all-India rural poverty at 25.7% and urban at 13.7% (2011-12 data).
Crucial for Prelims; sparked massive public debate on low poverty lines.
Higher poverty line than Tendulkar. Rural MPCE at Rs. 972 and Urban MPCE at Rs. 1407 per month (2011-12).
Separated normative food requirement and non-food essential expenses using alternative methodology (reference period FRP/MRP).
Tested for comparative analysis against Tendulkar committee recommendations.

items.definition: An NSSO survey method where consumer expenditure data is collected for a 30-day recall period for all items.
A methodology where expenditure data is gathered using a 365-day recall period for low-frequency items (clothing, education, institutional healthcare) and 30-day for remaining items.
Recall period utilizing 7-day for edible oil, eggs, fruits, vegetables, meat; 30-day for other food, fuel, miscellaneous; 365-day for durable goods, clothing, and education.
Lakdawala Committee (1993), Tendulkar Committee (2009), Rangarajan Committee (2014), Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog) nodal oversight.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Inter-state Disparities**: Higher poverty concentration persists in central and eastern Indian states (Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh).
• **Rural-Urban Divide**: While absolute poverty has declined, the depth of urban poverty and disguised unemployment in rural agriculture remain key structural challenges.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Delays in comprehensive consumer expenditure surveys, debate over normative versus behavioral baskets, and inflation indexing.
• **Policy Interventions**: Shift towards NITI Aayog's Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) based on NFHS data capturing health, education, and standard of living directly.

items.title: Mnemonic for Chronological Order of Poverty Committees
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "ALways Taste Real Food" (AL-T-R-F)
• **Decoded Meaning**: **Alagh** (1979) -> **Lakdawala** (1993) -> **Tendulkar** (2009) -> **Rangarajan** (2014).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly solves chronological arrangement questions in UPSC Prelims.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember that Tendulkar moved away from calories to consumption basket with health/education, while Rangarajan raised the bar even higher.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often traps candidates by stating that the Tendulkar or Rangarajan committees were appointed by the Ministry of Finance. They were actually appointed by the Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog).

Mains Value Addition: In Mains answers on poverty, critique the monetary-metric approach and advocate for NITI Aayog's Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) aligned with SDG Target 1.2 to show contemporary administrative awareness.

keyTakeaways: Poverty estimation in India evolved from pure nutritional calorie benchmarks to comprehensive consumption expenditure baskets including health and education.
The chronological sequence of expert groups—Alagh, Lakdawala, Tendulkar, and Rangarajan—represents progressive methodological refinement.
Contemporary policy discourse has transitioned from mere income/consumption poverty lines to multidimensional deprivation indices like NITI Aayog's MPI.
